JMIC# 00 1-26 Regional Threat Level : CRITICAL
1. Operational Summary – Last 72 Hours
Arabian Gulf & Strait of Hormuz
Strait of Hormuz traffic remains significantly reduced. On 03 May 2026, UKMTO received a report
of an incident 11NM west of Sirik, Iran, in which the Master of a northbound bulk carrier reported
being attacked by multiple small craft. The vessel departed the area and all crew are reported safe.
Anchorages show no significant change in congestion. Reports of mines in and near the TSS persist,
and GNSS interference remains sporadic but reduced from the level of activity recorded in March.
Gulf of Oman & Arabian Sea (No change)
Merchant vessels continue to report a strong naval presence. Blockade enforcement activity is
reported in the area and mariners are advised to maintain prudent standoff distance from naval
units. For ships carrying humanitarian cargos destined for Iran, JMIC has released Advisory 003-
26 detailing coordination requirements for review and approval.
No new verified incidents affecting commercial shipping have been reported in the last 72 hours.
Southern Red Sea, Bab el Mandeb & Gulf of Aden (No change)
Commercial traffic remains steady in the Bab el Mandeb and Gulf of Aden. Houthi messaging
continues without associated operational indicators.
Somali Coast and Somali Basin
Piracy threat level remains SEVERE. An oil products tanker continues to be held by pirates on the
northeastern Somali coast, and a general cargo ship remains held south of Eyl. No injuries have
been reported in either case, and there are no verified updates indicating movement, release, or
escalation.
In the last 72 hours, a tanker reported an approach by a suspected Pirate Action Group
approximately 500 NM east of Somalia. The skiff closed to within 400 m before disengaging; no
injuries or damage were reported. Extended-range PAG operations enabled by motherships
(hijacked dhows) are an active threat.
Three additional reports were issued regarding activity in vicinity of the Gulf of Aden:
• 01 May (UKMTO 048-26): A bulk carrier reported a black-hulled skiff with seven armed
persons approaching approximately 92 NM SW of Al Mukalla.
• 02 May (UKMTO 049-26): A bulk carrier reported a green-hulled skiff, accompanied by a
white fishing vessel, approaching to within 500 m approximately 84 NM SW of Al
Mukalla.
1
• 02 May, a tanker was boarded by armed personnel ~10nm off the coast of Yemen. The crew
is detained by the attackers and is currently underway towards Somalia.
Vessels transiting the region are advised to maintain heightened vigilance, apply BMP-MS
measures, and report any suspicious activity to UKMTO.
Northern Red Sea & Suez Canal (No change)
No confirmed attacks or disruptions. Suez Canal transits continue normally. Electronic interference
remains sporadic.
Eastern Mediterranean (No change)
No maritime attacks have been reported. Periodic electronic and navigational interference continues
near Cyprus and the Levant. Naval presence remains elevated, and vessels are advised to maintain
prudent separation from military units. An aid flotilla originating from Barcelona continues enroute
Gaza. Vessels in vicinity of the aid flotilla should consider media activity likely as it travels east.
---

3. Maritime Incidents & Traffic Assessment
3A. Confirmed Vessel Incidents (Since 1 March) (No change)
Total of 37 incidents since 1 March; no new confirmed vessel incidents in the last 48 hours.
3B. Infrastructure Incidents (Last 72 Hours) (No change)
No attacks on ports or maritime infrastructure reported. Overall risk remains SUBSTANTIAL,
driven by the potential for renewed kinetic activity and ongoing uncertainty around Iranian coastal
waters and blockade-related enforcement.
3C. Traffic Trends
• Strait of Hormuz:
o Historical average: ~138 vessels/day
o 30 April: 10 transits
o 01 May: 15 transits
o 02 May: 9 transits
• Bab el-Mandeb:
o 104 vessel transits in past 72 hours
o Still below pre-2023 baseline
* Metrics are a compilation of data from S&P Maritime and SeaVision sources.
3D. Port & Anchorage Congestion (No change)
High vessel density persists across major Arabian Gulf anchorages, with no significant change in
congestion levels over the last 72 hours. Traffic patterns remain largely unchanged as operators
continue to delay Strait of Hormuz transits in response to observed activity.
Vessels operating in crowded anchorages should maintain heightened situational awareness and
monitor for any navigational degradation to reduce collision risk. Periodic repositioning within
anchorages remains advisable to avoid predictability and reduce exposure to potential targeting.
3E. GNSS / AIS Interference (No change)
GNSS interference remains sporadic and localized across the Strait of Hormuz approaches, the Gulf
of Oman, the Arabian Gulf, the central Red Sea, and the Suez Canal approaches. AIS reliability in
the Arabian Gulf reflects overall improvement since 15 March.
---
4. Outlook (24–48 Hours)
Arabian Gulf / Strait of Hormuz (No change)
The operating environment remains high risk. Security pressure around the SOH is expected to
persist, with aggressive hailing and assertive action by Iranian units. The ceasefire remains fragile,
and blockade-related enforcement activity continues. Rapid, short-notice actions near Iranian
coastal waters, anchorages, and predictable routing points remain possible. The TSS and adjacent
waters may have associated mine risk based upon various reports.
3
Gulf of Oman / Arabian Sea (No change)
Naval activity remains elevated in the area. Verification hails and queries for vessels approaching
the Strait of Hormuz or moving to/from Iranian ports is highly likely. Operators may encounter
suspicious approaches and electronic interference near coastal transit lanes.
Southern Red Sea / Bab el Mandeb / Gulf of Aden (No change)
Houthi messaging continues without associated operational indicators. The potential for renewed
disruption persists should regional tensions escalate. GNSS interference remains a residual hazard,
with effects from the central Red Sea periodically extending into the southern sector.
Somali Coast and Somali Basin
There is a critical risk of pirate activity in the region. Two vessels are held, another vessel was take
in Yemeni territorial waters, and several recent suspicious approaches are noted. PAG activity is
assessed as highly likely across both the Somali Coast and Somali Basin, supported by weather
conditions favourable for small-boat operations. Mariners should maintain a vigilant watch and
report any suspicious activity to UKMTO and MSCIO.
Northern Red Sea / Suez (No change)
The environment remains stable with no indicators of maritime escalation. Periodic EMI and GNSS
disruptions are likely to continue.
Eastern Mediterranean (No change)
While there is no major change in the Eastern Mediterranean, periodic electronic and navigational
interference may be encountered near Cyprus and the Levant. Naval presence remains elevated, and
vessels should maintain prudent separation from military units. Operators should maintain
awareness of the Gaza aid flotilla and associated media interest.
---
